hook: The Mughal emperor who built the Taj Mahal for the wife he loved.

pages.x: Prince Khurram was born in Lahore in 1592, a grandson of Akbar. A brilliant general, he was given the title Shah Jahan, "King of the World", by his father, then rebelled against him. He became emperor in 1628.

At 15 he was engaged to Arjumand Banu Begum, and married her five years later. She became Mumtaz Mahal, "jewel of the palace", his constant companion, who rode with him even on campaigns. They had 14 children.
In 1631 she died giving birth to their 14th child. Shah Jahan was so stricken, it is said, that his hair turned white within months, and for two years he gave up music and fine clothes.

He built her a tomb of white marble at Agra, beside the Yamuna river. About 20,000 workers and 1,000 elephants worked on it for some 20 years, and its walls were inlaid with precious stones from all over Asia.

He built a new capital, Shahjahanabad, now Old Delhi, with the Red Fort and the great Jama Masjid. He sat on the Peacock Throne, covered with gold and jewels, said to have cost twice as much as the Taj.

In 1658, when he fell ill, his sons fought for the throne. The winner, Aurangzeb, locked his father in Agra Fort for his last eight years. Legend says he spent them gazing across the river at the Taj Mahal. He was buried beside Mumtaz.
Shah Jahan's reign was the golden age of Mughal building. The Taj Mahal, his monument to love, is one of the wonders of the world.
pts: Built the Red Fort and Old Delhi
Ruled the Mughal Empire at its richest
